meta.title: Rondje · a regular walk with a dog who's waiting for you
meta.description: Rondje connects young adults with dogs from neighbours and shelters that could really use an extra walk. Free and safe, in the Netherlands, Belgium and Spain.

footer.tagline: Rondje is a free platform that puts walkers, owners and shelters in touch. Rondje itself is not a party to any arrangements made.
footer.demo: Demo mode: no database is connected yet. Data is not saved.

home.title: A regular walk with a dog <mark>who's waiting for you.</mark>
home.lede: Rondje connects young adults with the dogs of neighbours who can't walk far any more, and with shelter dogs. Free, safe and good for you both.
home.how1: Create a profile with a photo and say a bit about yourself.
home.how2: Choose a dog and request a first meeting. The owner or the shelter is always there.
home.how3: Hit it off? Then you can walk the dog on your own. The owner can see where you are, live.
home.how4: Go for a regular walk every week. Afterwards, tell us privately how it went.
home.forWalkersText: Time outdoors, a regular plan and a dog who's happy to see you. Aged 18 and over, free of charge.
home.forOwnersText: Can't walk far any more? You decide who walks your dog, for how long, and whether treats are allowed. Family can sign you up too.
home.forSheltersText: Put all your dogs online in one go, plan supervised group walks and get a regular group of young volunteers.
home.safetyTitle: Trust is built step by step
home.safety1: The first time, you always walk together with the owner or the shelter.
home.safety2: ID is checked in person at the first meeting. Rondje doesn't keep a copy.
home.safety3: Solo walks are only possible once the owner allows them for that dog, and after the safety quiz.
home.safety4: During the walk, the owner can see live where the dog is. The route is deleted after 30 days.
home.safety5: After every walk, both sides give private feedback. Concerns go to our team, not to the other person.
home.safety6: You can always report or block someone. Anyone who breaks the rules is removed from the platform.
home.countriesText: Rondje works in the Netherlands, Belgium and Spain, in Dutch, French, Spanish and English.
home.freeTitle: Free, and it'll stay that way
home.freeText: No ads, no subscription, and we never sell data. Rondje runs on voluntary support, and later on partners and funds that stick to our rules.

quiz.title: Safety quiz
quiz.lede: Eight questions about walking safely. All correct? Then you can request solo walks.
quiz.passed: Passed! You can now request solo walks with owners who allow them.
quiz.failed: Almost. Take another look at the questions in red.

heat.q: It's 28 degrees. What do you do?
heat.a0: Just walk as usual, dogs cope well with heat
heat.a1: A short walk in the shade, bring water, and feel the pavement with your hand to check it isn't too hot
heat.a2: Have a good run, so it's over sooner

leash.q: Can the dog go off the leash?
leash.a0: Only if the owner has explicitly allowed it, and only where it's permitted
leash.a2: Yes, if the dog listens well

treats.q: You have a treat in your pocket. Can you give it?
treats.a2: Only if the profile says it's allowed

otherDogs.q: Another dog comes towards you. What do you do?
otherDogs.a0: Let them have a good sniff
otherDogs.a1: Keep your distance, ask the other owner first, and calmly walk on if you're unsure

escaped.q: The dog has got loose. What do you do first?
escaped.a0: Stay calm, don't chase or shout after the dog, and call the owner straight away
escaped.a1: Search yourself first, and only then call the owner

bite.q: The dog bites another dog. What do you do?
bite.a2: Make sure everyone is safe, exchange details, call the owner and report it in Rondje

stress.q: The dog yawns a lot, licks its lips and pulls away. What does that mean?
stress.a1: It's not feeling at ease; find a quieter spot

overdue.q: You're heading back later than agreed. What do you do?
overdue.a0: Let the owner know straight away
overdue.a1: Nothing, the app shows it anyway

safety.title: How Rondje handles safety
safety.lede: People don't hand their dog to just anyone. That's why we build trust step by step, and keep the platform clean.
safety.level1: New account: you can request a first meeting or join a supervised group walk.
safety.level2: After the first meeting: the owner has seen your ID in person and can allow solo walks for that one dog.
safety.level3: After the safety quiz: you can request solo walks with owners who allow them.
safety.duringText: Your phone shares your location with the owner while the walk is on. If it runs over, you both get a notification. The help button shows you straight away who to call.
safety.afterText: Both sides give private feedback. Reports of an injured or stressed dog, or of someone feeling unsafe, go straight to our team.
safety.fraudText: Rondje is free, so anyone asking for money stands out. Messages with payment requests, bank account numbers or links are flagged. Shelters are checked using their KvK, KBO or CIF number. Anyone who mistreats a dog or a person is blocked and reported where necessary.
safety.liabilityText: Rondje puts people in touch and is not itself a party to the arrangement. The owner remains liable for any damage the dog causes and must be insured for it. We recommend that walkers take out their own liability insurance. Read the terms for all the details.
safety.reportText: Report it using the ‘Report’ button on a profile, dog or walk. We'll look into it within 24 hours.

support.eyebrow: Free, and it stays that way
support.title: Make Rondje possible
support.lede: Rondje is free for walkers, owners and shelters, and it will stay that way. Still, keeping Rondje safe and online costs money. Here is how that works.

promise.free: Rondje stays free for everyone: no subscription, no paywall, no premium version.
promise.data: We never sell data, and never share it for marketing.
promise.sponsors: A sponsor or partner never decides which dogs or people you see.
promise.equal: Supporters get no priority and no extras. Everyone uses Rondje the same way.

support.costsLede: An honest estimate, from now to a bigger Rondje. The more people use Rondje, the more it costs.

hosting.label: Website and app

support.costsNote: Estimate, updated on {date}. We keep costs as low as we can.
support.giveText: A small monthly contribution helps cover the costs. Contributions go to {operator}, who builds and runs Rondje.
support.giveNote: You pay through {platform}, under their terms. A contribution is voluntary, not tax-deductible, and gives no benefits in Rondje.
support.giveSoon: Soon you will be able to support Rondje here with a small contribution. Until then, everything below helps a lot too.

help.tip: Know a shelter where dogs could use more walks? Let us know.
help.invite: Know someone who would love to walk a dog, or a neighbour with a dog? Send your personal link.
help.share: Share a photo of your walk on social media, with the owner's permission.
help.shareInstagram: Share a photo of your walk and tag @{handle}, with the owner's permission.
help.partner: A pet shop, insurer, municipality or fund that wants to help? Great, with clear rules: no ads and no say in who you see.

free.a: Because money should never stop anyone from getting outside together, whether young people or older people with a dog. That is why nobody pays to use Rondje.

where.a: To {operator}, for the costs above: hosting, database, maps, the apps and materials for shelters. Anything left goes into building Rondje further and making it known.

tax.a: No. Rondje is not (yet) a registered charity, so you cannot deduct a contribution from your taxes.

perks.q: Do I get anything in return?
perks.a: No, on purpose. Supporters get no priority, no extra features and no say in matching or moderation. You do get our thanks, and an update now and then.

sponsors.a: Yes, if they stick to our rules: no ads in Rondje, no data, and no say in which dogs or people are visible. A sponsor could, for example, pay for poo bags for shelters.

about.title: A walk together, good for you and for a dog
about.lede: Rondje connects young adults with dogs that want to get out more: from neighbours who can no longer walk their dog well, and from shelters.
about.why1: Many young people love being outside and love dogs, but cannot have one themselves. At the same time, older people and people who are ill cannot walk their dog as often as they would like. And in shelters, every dog is waiting for one more walk.
about.why2: A regular walk with a dog is good for everyone: exercise, fresh air and a chat with a neighbour. Rondje makes that easy, safe and free.
about.why3: Rondje is not care or therapy. Not feeling well? The help page shows where you can turn.

how.meet: The first time, you always meet the owner and the dog together. Only after that may you walk alone, if the owner agrees.
how.adults: Everyone who walks is 18 or older and first takes a short safety quiz.
how.shelters: At shelters you walk in supervised group walks, at times the shelter chooses.
how.free: Rondje is free. Nobody asks for or pays money for a walk.

walker.1: On warm days bring water, and feel with your hand whether the pavement is too hot for their paws.
walker.2: Let a dog sniff your hand before you pet it. That's how you introduce yourself.
walker.3: Sniffing tires a dog as much as running. A calm sniffing walk is a gift.
walker.4: Ears back and a low tail? Give the dog some space and talk calmly.
walker.5: In the dark? A light on the leash makes you both easier to see.
walker.6: Walk at your own pace. A dog that pulls learns more from you standing still than from pulling back.
walker.7: Sitting on a bench together counts too. Walks don't have to be fast or far.
walker.8: Another dog coming? Ask its owner first whether they may say hello.
walker.9: Walking in the morning? It's quieter and cooler then, nice for older dogs.
walker.10: Tell the owner something nice about the walk afterwards. It makes their day.

owner.1: Note what your dog finds scary, like bikes or other dogs. Then a walker knows what to look out for.
owner.2: Put the leash, poo bags and a treat ready by the door. Then the walk can start right away.
owner.3: A fixed moment each week makes it easy, for you, your dog and the walker.
owner.4: The first time, you walk together. Show how your dog likes to walk and where they always stop.
owner.5: A photo of your dog looking into the camera attracts more walkers than one from behind.
owner.6: Follow the walk live, or let go and read the report afterwards.
owner.7: Let the walker know you're happy afterwards. A thank-you keeps a regular buddy.
owner.8: Is there a notice board at the supermarket? A flyer with your link brings walkers from your own neighbourhood.

profileHub.inviteShort: Know someone who loves walking, or someone with a dog? Share your own link.
profileHub.supportText: Free and ad-free. See how you can help.
profileHub.tipText: Know a shelter or someone with a dog who could use help?
profileHub.shelterText: Work at a shelter? Put your dogs online here.

discover.title: Who’s coming along today?
discover.levelTop: Top level. What a lot of walks!
discover.badges: {n, plural, =0 {No badges yet} one {# badge} other {# badges}}
discover.groupWalksText: Guided, at a shelter. A nice way to start.

launch.title: Launch hub
launch.lede: Everything for the launch in one place: what is left, who does what, your messages and how it grows. At your own pace.
launch.install: Tip: open this page on your iPhone in Safari and choose Share → Add to Home Screen. The launch hub then opens as its own app.

entry.title: Launch hub
entry.text: Launch list, message bank for shelters and others, weekly numbers and costs.

waiting.title: Waiting for Laurens
waiting.hint: Only you can do these four. After that, the rest goes faster on its own.

task.autoHint: This ticks itself off as soon as it shows in the real data.

name.title: Choose the name: Woofmigo, yes or no
name.hint: First check in App Store Connect whether the name is free (Apps → + → New App), and search TMview for WOOF and MIGO in classes 9, 42 and 45. Until then everything stays on Brand.name and APP_NAME.

goLive.title: Go live: merge to production
goLive.hint: PR #3 and the parity PR, with migrations 0007 and 0008. Follow “Live zetten” in CLAUDE.md: local checks green, Vercel preview Ready, then squash-merge. Ticks itself off once this hub runs in production.

submit.title: Submit to Apple
submit.hint: In App Store Connect, with the text from docs/app-store/vermelding.md and a test account for the review. You submit it yourself.

money.title: Everything that costs money
money.hint: Apple Developer (€99 a year) and the domain. Your approval and your payment: Claude buys nothing.

sendThree.title: Send your first 3 e-mails
sendThree.hint: Pick 3 shelters under Contacts, add the e-mail address, tap "Open in mail" and send from your own mail. Then mark them "sent".

trademark.title: Trademark check on TMview
trademark.hint: Search for “rondje” or the new name, in classes 9, 42 and 45.

appleAccount.title: Apple Developer account
appleAccount.hint: Needed to submit, for Sign in with Apple and for HealthKit. €99 a year; counts in the costs once you tick it off.

domain.title: Buy and connect a domain
domain.hint: After choosing the name, about €12 a year. Then Vercel → Settings → Domains (docs/LAUNCH.md §8). Counts in the costs once you tick it off.

socialKeys.title: Keys for Sign in with Apple and Google
socialKeys.hint: Follow docs/LAUNCH.md §5 and add them in Vercel. Ticks itself off once both are on.

healthkit.title: Turn on the HealthKit capability
healthkit.hint: For the App ID app.rondje.mobile on developer.apple.com, and in Xcode under Signing & Capabilities.

legal.title: Legal check
legal.hint: Have a lawyer go through docs/legal/REVIEW.md. Only launch after the legal entity exists.

analytics.title: Turn on Vercel Web Analytics
analytics.hint: In the Vercel dashboard: project rondje → Analytics → Enable. Free on the Hobby plan, within its limits.

privacy.title: Update the privacy policy
privacy.hint: Add Apple Health (HealthKit) and the website statistics, via the lawyer.

firstMails.title: Email the first 10 shelters
firstMails.hint: With the message bank below. Ticks itself off at 10 shelters on “sent” or further.

firstDemo.title: First call with a shelter
firstDemo.hint: Ticks itself off once a shelter in your contacts is on “meeting”.

firstDog.title: First real dog online
firstDog.hint: From a real shelter or owner, without the Example label. Ticks itself off.

blobCleanup.title: Also delete photos and routes from Blob after 30 days
blobCleanup.hint: So the privacy promise also holds for Vercel Blob (see STAND.md).

storeTexts.title: App Store text and screenshots with the chosen name
storeTexts.hint: After choosing the name: fill it in in docs/app-store/vermelding.md and make new screenshots.

mountAnalytics.title: Add the visitor counter to the site
mountAnalytics.hint: The Analytics component is ready and still has to go into the layout. No cookies; admin pages are not counted.

game.title: Progress
game.top: Highest level. Every step still counts.
game.routeTitle: On the way to the first real walk
game.noPressure: No streaks and no rush: points only come from what is done, and nothing is ever taken away.

composer.title: Message bank
composer.hint: Pick a message, fill in the fields and open it in your own mail app, or copy the text. Rondje never sends anything itself.
composer.noEmail: This contact has no valid email address: your mail app opens without a recipient.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.hint: Business contact details only, and only here in the database. Only change the status after you sent or heard something yourself. Delete a contact when you no longer need it.
contacts.empty: No contacts yet. Start with the first shelter.

errors.invalid: Fill in at least a name or an organisation.
errors.email: This email address is not right.

contacts.prepareHint: The nearest shelters from the shelter list, with their website in the note. Fill in the e-mail address yourself; nothing is sent.
contacts.prepared: {n, plural, =0 {No new shelters found: they are already here.} one {# shelter ready. Add the e-mail address and write your message.} other {# shelters ready. Add the e-mail addresses and write your messages.}}

numbers.title: Numbers per week
numbers.hint: Only counts from real data, without names, for the last 8 weeks. Example data and admins do not count.

visits.title: Website visits
visits.text: Counting visitors starts once you turn on Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard (project rondje → Analytics → Enable). On the free Hobby plan it costs nothing, within Vercel’s limits. The numbers then show in the dashboard.
visits.privacy: No cookies. Admin pages, links with codes and the app shell are not counted.

costs.title: Costs per month
costs.hint: What Rondje costs now. Yearly amounts are shown per month; they only count once the matching task is ticked off.
costs.walksPerActiveHint: Walks in the last 30 days, divided by the walkers who walked then.
costs.members: {n, plural, one {# real member} other {# real members}}
